- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 10–15 days), then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 81.20 → 82.31 → 84.34), leading to overcorrection or failure to capture sustained momentum.
- Underestimates when true price moves downward after a peak (e.g., 83.26 → 82.64 → 81.82), failing to recognize mean reversion or short-term correction.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the first 5–7 days, then gradually adjust downward — suggesting a lag in recognizing recent price trends.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices, especially when history shows consolidation or minor volatility — overreacting to noise.
- When true price exceeds forecast by >5% in early days, model tends to undercorrect later — suggesting a failure to account for momentum decay.
- Forecasts often fail to capture the “tail” of a price run — i.e., the final 5–7 days where true price may dip or stabilize, while model continues upward.
